{{Short description|Mathematical space}}
In [[mathematics]], especially in [[real algebraic geometry]], a '''semialgebraic space''' is a space which is locally [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] to a [[semialgebraic set]].

==Definition==
Let ''U'' be an open subset of '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> for some ''n''. A '''semialgebraic function''' on ''U'' is defined to be a [[continuous function|continuous]] [[real number|real]]-valued function on ''U'' whose restriction to any [[semialgebraic set]] contained in ''U'' has a [[graph of a function|graph]] which is a semialgebraic subset of the product space '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>×'''R'''. This endows '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> with a sheaf <math>\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{R}^n}</math> of semialgebraic functions.

(For example, any polynomial mapping between semialgebraic sets is a [[semialgebraic function]], as is the maximum of two semialgebraic functions.)  

A '''semialgebraic space''' is a [[locally ringed space]] <math>(X, \mathcal{O}_X)</math> which is locally isomorphic to '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> with its sheaf of semialgebraic functions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Delfs |first1=Hans |last2=Knebusch |first2=Manfred |title=Semialgebraic Topology over a Real Closed Field II: Basic Theory of Semialgebraic Spaces |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |date=1981 |volume=178 |issue=2 |pages=175-213 |url=https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/12798/1/ubr05114_ocr.pdf |access-date=17 March 2026}}</ref>
